paragraphs.source_en:
Jane’s reply, dated 6 July from Villa Magni, has a postscript which certainly suggests the
‘coquette’ of the first line of Bright wanderer, fair coquette of Heaven: ‘Why do you talk of
never enjoying moments like the past, are you going to join your friend Plato or do you
expect I shall do soon?’ (Gisborne Jnl 161) Cameron comments that ‘this exchange, taken
in conjunction with Jane’s letters to Williams and Shelley’s poems to Jane, indicates that
there was no actual love affair but that Shelley was seriously turning toward Jane and that
Jane was not quite closing the door on him’ (Golden Years 305). The unresolvable question
that remains is, at what stage had this rapidly developing situation arrived by the time S.
left on his last journey? S. had by the beginning of July presented several poems to Jane
which deal directly with his feelings for her, and it is certain that Mary remained unaware
